Ephemera ephemera.space

Every eight hours, SpaceX publishes where each Starlink satellite is going, with its uncertainty. It is the only public feed of its kind. Each set is replaced by the next. Ephemera keeps the history.

The archive record

As of 2026-09-03 16:20 UTC the archive holds 15 cycles. 15 are complete with Merkle roots and 15 are anchored in Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps. Raw data kept: 336 GB. Poller heartbeat coverage: 100.0% of the last 24 hours. Cadence holds (a manifest served longer than 9 hours): 1. This project exists because SpaceX publishes the feed openly.

Method: built from each cycle's cycle.json and witness.json in the poller's spool; coverage is the fraction of the last 24 h's minutes with a watcher heartbeat under 10 minutes old (D18); a cadence hold is a manifest first-seen gap over 9 h. Poller: home (Cape Town, residential; single poller until poller A exists). Full data: ledger.json; the verification procedure a stranger can run is in the repository's VERIFY.md (independent Merkle re-implementation, OpenTimestamps against a Bitcoin block, Wayback copies re-hashed).

Catalogue visibility

How far the public catalogue's prediction sits from the operator's, for every satellite in a cycle. The public element set (Space-Track) is propagated with SGP4 to the operator file's own epochs, every 360 minutes across the file's span, and the distance is taken. Both are predictions. The operator's file includes planned trajectory changes the public set cannot know about, so a large distance is that gap, not an error of the satellite. Public GP data is too noisy to test sub-metre covariance; the self-consistency scoreboard, when it exists, measures prediction-versus-later-prediction.

Latest scored cycle a39dfdfee0fd (first seen 2026-09-03 12:09 UTC): 11,090 of 11,117 files scored against the snapshot fetched 2026-09-03 10:10 UTC (12811 element sets); 27 without a public set, 0 marked decayed, 0 propagation failures, 0 unreadable. Mean element age across the comparison: 51.2 h. Scored 2026-09-03 13:26 UTC. See it on the globe: every satellite drawn twice, the operator trajectory and the public catalogue's ghost.

Method: Public element set (Space-Track gp snapshot) propagated with SGP4 (skyfield 1.55, python-sgp4 2.27; TEME to GCRS by Skyfield, taken as J2000) and differenced against the operator-published trajectory (EME2000) at the file's own record epochs every 360 min. Distance in km; components in the operator's radial/in-track/cross-track frame; altitude is geocentric radius minus 6378.137 km; element age is evaluation epoch minus element-set epoch, signed. Both inputs are predictions; the operator's includes planned trajectory changes the public set cannot know about.

Operator ephemerides are predictions, not observations. Inputs are archived by this project and witnessed by OpenTimestamps and the Wayback Machine; they are not re-fetchable from the source after one cycle. Every figure above carries the build time it was true at. Gapped or lost items are printed, never hidden.
